L80: # Clinical Studies
L81: 
L82: Red Bank Veterinary Hospital’ veterinarians and patients participate in a variety of clinical studies.
L83: 
L84: At Red Bank Veterinary Hospital, our veterinarians participate in clinical studies initiated by our teams across a variety of medical specialties as well as studies in collaboration with other institutions.
L85: 
L86: Much is gained from participation in these studies: veterinarians obtain new techniques, treatments, and knowledge; and pets live longer, healthier lives through better care.
L87: For additional information on current and pending clinical studies please see below or contact us at (732) 747-3636.
L88: ## View Our Current Clinical Studies For Pets
L89: 
L90: ### Feline Heart Disease Study: Cats
L91: 
L92: July 30th, 2025
L93: ### Objective:
L94: 
L95: Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) has caused suffering in cats for too long. This study is seeking non-diabetic feline patients who have had their first CHF episode in the last 60 days and are currently stable. This clinical trial is a double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate an investigational medication with the goal of seeking regulatory approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).
L96: 
L97: Cats may qualify if they are:
L98:   * Diagnosed within the last 60 days
L99: 
L100:   * Not diabetic and not on insulin
L101: 
L102:   * At least 12 months of age
L103: 
L104:   * Weigh at least 4.4 lbs (2 kg)
L105: 
L106:   * Currently clinically stable (free of pleural effusion/pulmonary edema)
L107: 
L108:   * Not pregnant, lactating, or intended for breeding
L109: 
L110: Everything required by the study is provided at no cost to owners of enrolled feline patients, including:
L111: 
L112:   * Cardiac and respiratory exams
L113:   * Diagnostic tests, including echocardiogram (echo), electrocardiogram (ECG/EKG), thoracic radiography (x-ray), and systolic blood pressure (SBP)
L114: 
L115:   * Bloodwork, including hematology, biochemistry, total thyroxine, fructosamine, NT-proBNP
L116: 
L117:   * Urinalysis
L118: ### Inclusion Criteria:
L119: 
L120: To be eligible, the following criteria must apply:
L121: 
L122: [1]a. Diagnosis at Screening Visit or history of primary HCM/HOCM:
L123: 
L124:   * the size of the interventricular septum (IVSd) and/or the left ventricular free wall thickness in diastole (LVFWd) is ≥ 6 mm
L125: 
L126:   * HOCM cats are characterized by a systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve coupled with diffuse left ventricular (LV) outflow tract turbulence
L127: b. other phenotypes of primary cardiomyopathy: diagnosed based on criteria of ACVIM consensus statement.
L128: 
L129: [2] Diagnosis of a first congestive heart failure episode (ACVIM Consensus Statement [7] Stage C) in the last 60 days as a result of a review of the radiographic or ultrasonographic imaging that was obtained at the time of CHF diagnosis with pulmonary edema or pleural effusion at the discretion of the Investigator
L130: [3] Cat is clinically stable at enrollment (i.e., normal respiration (e.g., no effort to breathe, bright/alert/responsive, on oral medication, and under owner care)) at the Investigator’s discretion
L131: 
L132: [4] Signed Owner Informed Consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation
L133: 
L134: [5] Age: ≥ 12 months at Screening Visit
L135: 
L136: [6] Body weight ≥ 4.4 lbs/2.0 kg at Screening Visit
L137: ### Non-inclusion criteria:
L138: 
L139: The cat is not eligible if one or more of the following criteria applies:
L140: 
L141: [1] Current or past treatment with a SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g., velagliflozin, bexagliflozin)
L142: 
L143: [2] Treatment with furosemide doses ≥10 mg/kg per day or torasemide doses ≥0.6mg/kg per day at Screening Visit
L144: [3] Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus in the past or at Screening Visit (e.g., serum fructosamine above reference range of central laboratory, detection of glucosuria) or under treatment with any anti-diabetic drugs
L145: 
L146: [4] Current treatment with any drugs listed under “Prohibited concomitant treatment”
L147: 
L148: [5] Heart diseases other than primary cardiomyopathy (e.g., congenital heart diseases, taurine deficiency, or potential neoplastic diseases such as cardiac lymphoma, etc.)
L149: [6] Arrhythmias that require medical therapy at the discretion of the Investigator (e.g., atrial fibrillation, 3rd-degree atrioventricular (AV) Block)
L150: 
L151: [7] History or presenting with clinical signs of feline arterial thromboembolism (FATE) at Screening Visit
L152: 
L153: [8] Detection of intracardiac thrombi via echocardiography at Screening Visit
L154: [9] Hyperthyroidism (i.e., total thyroxine (TT4) level above reference range of central laboratory) or cats currently receiving medication or dietary treatment for hyperthyroidism at Screening Visit
L155: 
L156: [10] Systemic arterial hypertension (systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg) at Screening Visit
L157: 
L158: [11] Severe dehydration (e.g., considerable loss of skin turgor, enophthalmos, dry mucous membranes, weak/thready pulses, systemic hypotension, or altered level of consciousness) at Screening Visit
L159: [12] Moderate to severe renal failure (blood creatinine value ≥ 251 µmol/L or ≥ 2.9 mg/dL) at Screening Visit and known primary renal dysfunction in the judgment of the Investigator
L160: 
L161: [13] Concurrent chronic lower respiratory diseases (e.g., feline asthma) at Screening Visit
L162: 
L163: [14] Persistent diarrhea (duration > 7 days) in the last 14 days before Screening Visit
L164: [15] Other concomitant disease/condition (e.g., acromegaly, cachexia, neoplasia, systemic infection, anemia, or known heart worm infection/disease) that might interfere with the study results
L165: 
L166: [16] Pregnant, lactating, or intended for breeding
L167: 
L168: [17] Ongoing participation in another study or previously enrolled in this study
L169: 
L170: Learn more by visiting: 【33†www.felineheartstudy.com†www.felineheartstudy.com】
L171: ### Dietary Treatment of Mild to Moderate Feline Chronic Enteropathy
L172: 
L173: JUN 04, 2019
L174: 
L175: *NOTE: This study is not currently enrolling new patients until further notice*
L176: The primary aim of the study is to assess the clinical responses of cats with naturally occurring mild to moderate chronic enteropathy when fed different types of dry kibble diets. As part of this study, three visits to Red Bank Veterinary Hospital in Tinton Falls are required for the patient. Owners must be willing to weigh the cat’s food daily for the entire 12 weeks.
L177: The owner will be required to fill out some screening paper work before making the appointment, as well as, complete a daily log of their cat’s habits for the duration of the study. The majority of the study is at no cost to the client.
L178: ### INCLUSION:
L179: 
L180:   * Cat must be 1-8 years old
L181: 
L182:   * Indoor only
L183: 
L184:   * Body Condition Score (BCS) 3-7/9
L185: 
L186:   * Must have recurring vomiting and/or small bowel diarrhea for > 3 weeks
L187: 
L188:   * Willing and able to eat 100% dry food with no wet food, “toppers”, or treats
L189: 
L190:   * No evidence of systemic illness
L191: 
L192:   * If found to be hypocobalaminemic (low in vitamin B12), the owner must be willing to follow the Texas A&M parenteral supplementation protocol, involving weekly and monthly injections.
L193:   * If a multicat household (up to 3 cats total), the owner must be able to feed all cats in the house the test diet. The owner must also be able to submit patient log information based on only the cat participating in the study.
L194: 
L195:   * All cats in the household must be dewormed with Panacur (fenbendazole) for 5 days within 1 month prior to study enrollment.
L196: 
L197:   * Cats that have undergone previous, but unsuccessful, medical treatment for gastrointestinal signs are still eligible.
L198: ### NON-INCLUSION:
L199: 
L200:   * History of constipation, tenesmus, hematochezia
L201: 
L202:   * Vomiting exclusively hairballs
L203: 
L204:   * Use of oral immunosuppressives within prior 3 weeks
L205: 
L206:   * Use of long acting immunosuppressives within prior 6 weeks
L207: 
L208:   * Use of antibiotics (e.g., tylosan, metronidazole) within prior 4 weeks
L209: 
L210:   * Use of probiotics within prior 4 weeks
L211: 
L212:   * History of > 10% unintentional weight loss within prior 2 months.
L213: ### OWNER INCENTIVES:
L214: 
L215:   * Initial Visit: Patient will receive a complimentary physical exam, complete blood count, chemistry with electrolytes, urinalysis, thyroxine level (T4), feline leukemia virus (FeLV), feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV), heartworm antigen and antibody, gastrointestinal (GI) panel, fecal test, abdominal x-rays and ultrasound at the initial visit. Some of these tests will not be repeated if they have been completed in the prior 4 weeks, nor will the owner be reimbursed.
L216:   * 4-week and 12 week rechecks: Patient will receive complimentary physical exams and recheck labwork.
L217: 
L218:   * Food will be provided at no cost for all cats in the home, regardless of participation in the study.
L219: ### COST TO CLIENT:
L220: 
L221: If the cat is hypocobalaminemic, cobalamin supplementation must be undertaken at the client’s own expense. Administration of Panacur prior to study enrollment is also at the client’s own expense.

L240: ### Pulmonic Stenosis (PS) Study: Cats & Dogs
L241: 
L242: JUN 04, 2019
L243: 
L244: Pulmonic stenosis is a birth defect in the heart. It is caused by an incomplete pulmonary valve on the right side of the heart. It can result in serious, life-threatening changes in the way that the heart pumps blood. This study will aim to collect data on procedural technique of the corrective surgery.
L245: ### OWNER INCENTIVES
L246: 
L247: Discounted charges for the procedure are the incentive. A free initial screening echocardiogram is included with the first visit. The client is responsible for all other charges including the initial standard exam fee.
L248: 
L249: ### CONTACT

L252:

L258: ### Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA): Cats & Dogs
L259: 
L260: JUN 04, 2019
L261: 
L262: Patent ductus arteriosus (also called PDA) is a birth defect in the heart. It is caused by incomplete changes in the heart’s circulation when a dog or cat is born. This results in serious, life-threatening changes in heart function and size. This study will aim to collect data on procedural technique of the corrective surgery.
L263: ### OWNER INCENTIVES
L264: 
L265: Discounted charges for the procedure are the incentive. A free initial screening echocardiogram is included with the first visit. The client is responsible for all other charges including the initial standard exam fee.
L266:

L277: ### Mitral Valve Disease Study: Dogs
L278: 
L279: JUN 04, 2019
L280: ### PURPOSE
L281: 
L282: To evaluate the relevance of history and presentation in the evaluation of chronic valve disease in small breed dogs.
L283: 
L284: ### CASE SELECTION
L285: 
L286: All dogs <20kg and older than 8 years with a significant systolic heart murmur. Study will cover a free echocardiogram.
L287: ### EXCLUSION CRITERIA
L288: 
L289:   * Dogs with other clinically relevant cardiac diseases (minor tricuspid valve disease will be included).
L290: 
L291:   * Dogs receiving antitussive medications (including corticosteroids, bronchodilators, cough suppressants).
L292: 
L293:   * Dogs receiving cardiac medications (pimobendan, enalapril, spironolactone).
L294: ### OWNER INCENTIVES
L295: 
L296: Clients will be responsible for some of the evaluation, but will be given a substantial discount.The following is provided by the Study at NO CHARGE to clients:
L297: 
L298:   * Echocardiogram
L299: 
L300:   * ECG
L301: 
L302: (A value of $794.33)
L303: 
L304: ### CLIENT RESPONSIBILITIES
L305: 
L306: Client is responsible for all other charges including, but not limited to:
L307: 
L308:   * Exam fee
L309: 
L310:   * Thoracic radiography (will not be repeated if adequate films already acquired)

L41: #
L42: 
L43: Canine Osteosarcoma Combined Immunotherapy Study (ECIP-OSA-01)
L44: 
L45: Enrollment for this study is closed.
L46: ### Study Overview
L47: ELIAS Animal Health is currently conducting a study to assess safety and efficacy of ELIAS’s vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant following surgery as a treatment for large-breed dogs newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma. The study, which is funded by grants from Morris Animal Foundation and Great Dane Club of America Charitable Trust, is being conducted in collaboration with Dr. Jeffrey Bryan and Dr. Megan Mickelson at the University of Missouri-Columbia.
L48: ### Study Summary
L49:   * Treatment includes amputation or limb-sparing surgery to remove primary tumor, followed by vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant.
L50:   * Patients must complete the 7-11 week protocol, conducted at the University of Missouri Veterinary School of Medicine, and return for periodic follow-up visits.
L51:   * Each patient will be monitored for 12 months post-diagnosis.
L52:   * Great Dane owners may qualify for additional financial assistance through the Great Dane Club of America.
L53: ### Key Inclusion Criteria
L54:   * Dog breeds eligible for this study include: Anatolian Shepherd, Bernese Mountain Dog, Boerboel, Cane Corso, Dogue de Bordeaux, Golden Retriever, Great Dane, Great Pyrenees, Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, Irish Wolfhound, Leonberger, Mastiff (all types), Newfoundland, Rottweiler, Saint Bernard, and Scottish Deerhound.
L55:   * Eligible patients must be newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma and must not have received prior treatment for the cancer.
L56:   * To qualify for limb-spare surgery, tumor must be in the distal radius or mid-ulnar location; no more than 1/3 radius may be affected.
L57:   * Eligible patients must not have metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis.
L58:   * Pet owner/caregiver must be able and willing to attend all treatment and follow-up visits at the Veterinary Health Center at the University of Missouri in Columbia, MO.
L59: *Additional inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.
L60: ### Participating Hospital: Veterinary Health Center at the University of Missouri-Columbia
L61: 
L62: Enrollment for this study is closed.
L63: 
L64: ECI^{®} is distributed under an Autologous Prescription Product license issued by the USDA.

L40: Clinical Study: ECI® Combined With Chemotherapy【17†jwiley】2026-01-27T13:32:14-06:00
L41: #
L42: 
L43: ECI® Combined with Chemotherapy for the Treatment of Canine Osteosarcoma
L44: 
L45: Contact ELIAS Animal Health for information or to discuss this treatment approach.
L46: 
L47: Some clinicians have expressed interest in using ECI^{®} as part of an integrated protocol that combines a minimized chemotherapy treatment followed by the ECI^{®} immunotherapy. In both human and veterinary oncology, the potential for combined treatments to produce better patient outcomes has been reported.
L48: ELIAS Animal Health is conducting prospective, open-label study to evaluate the efficacy of ECI^{®} combined with chemotherapy to treat bone cancer in dogs. Treatment includes one to four doses of chemotherapy after amputation followed by ECI^{®} immunotherapy. Dogs will be followed until death or lost to follow up to assess overall response rate and survival. No financial assistance is provided for participation in this study.
L49: ## Study Summary
L50:   * Eligible canine patients with newly diagnosed appendicular osteosarcoma will be treated with amputation, one to four doses of chemotherapy, and ECI®, a USDA-licensed autologous prescription product for treatment of osteosarcoma.
L51:   * Matched controls will be selected from a published data set in the National Cancer Institute’s Canine Data Commons.
L52:   * Kaplan-Meier analysis will be conducted with survival data compared to historical published results of dogs assigned to receive 4-dose carboplatin as treatment.
L53: ## Key Inclusion Criteria
L54: 
L55:   * Patients must be newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma and must not have received prior treatment for their osteosarcoma.
L56:   * Enrollment is required prior to amputation (affected limb must be intact).
L57:   * Eligible patients must not have metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis.
L58: 
L59: 【16†Contact us】 to learn more about this study and to see if your dog or canine patient may be a good candidate.
L60: ## Interim Results
L61: 
L62: Interim analysis of data from this study was presented at the 2025 Veterinary Cancer Society Annual Conference on September 26, 2025. The analysis assessed 21 dogs receiving one to four doses of chemotherapy followed 21 days later by ECI® versus 21 dogs (matched controls) receiving 4-dose carboplatin alone, which demonstrated one-year survival rates of 70% compared to 26%, respectively. Statistical significance (p < 0.05) was achieved with p = 0.012.
L63: The best responses were observed in the subgroup of dogs who received one dose of carboplatin followed 21 days later by ECI® (n=13) versus 4-dose carboplatin alone, which demonstrated one-year survival rates of 83% compared to 25%, respectively. Statistical significance (p < 0.05) was achieved with p = 0.002.
L64: 
L65: Additional research from this study will be available for reporting in mid-2026.
